image_transform: Whole views; aspect-preserving fit into common tiles, padding and identical labels. No flip or content crop.
cadence: All recorded frames retained; 10 control frames per playback second; display only.

notes.text: Keep the native grasp and key axis fixed; begin a gradual positive turn, watching tactile shape for resistance.
Contact remains round without a clear stop signal; continue turning gradually about the fixed vertical key axis.
Maintain grasp and insertion depth; continue the positive turn while checking for tactile resistance.
Continue gradual axial rotation; tactile contact remains circular and the key stays seated.
Maintain insertion depth and grip while continuing the turn; no clear tactile stop yet.
Continue turning about the seated key's vertical axis, maintaining grip and watching for a tactile deformation indicating resistance.
Keep the key seated and continue the positive axial turn; tactile patches remain round without a clear resistance signal.
Continue the gradual vertical-axis turn while holding position and native grip; monitor tactile deformation for the mechanical stop.
Reduce turn increments as the key approaches possible resistance, maintaining the seated position and native grasp.
Continue a small positive turn at fixed insertion depth; tactile contact remains round, so the stop is not yet clear.
Probe further with small axial turn increments, keeping grip and depth unchanged; monitor for the episode-specific stop.
Both tactile patches now show edge deformation consistent with resistance. Ease back slightly to unload torsion before a straight extraction.
Tactile deformation relaxed after the small backoff. Begin extracting straight upward, preserving orientation and the native grasp.
Test a very small straight pull, then pause; tactile contact shifted during the initial lift, so check for binding before extracting farther.
Continue a slow straight upward extraction with orientation and grip fixed; watch whether contact shear relaxes or grows.
Opposing tactile displacement is growing during the pull, suggesting binding. Return gently toward the seated depth to unload before refining the turn.
Ease back slightly farther at the seated depth to remove possible residual torsion before another straight pull.
Contact looks centered again after unloading torsion. Test a gentle straight upward pull at this refined angle, keeping the grasp unchanged.
Tactile contacts shift oppositely under the pull, suggesting continued binding. Unload the small lift and back off the turn slightly farther before retesting.
Contacts are nearly centered after unloading. Test a small straight upward extraction at the adjusted angle, maintaining the native grasp.
The small lift again displaced the tactile contacts. Unload back to the seated depth and reduce the turn slightly to locate the free extraction alignment.
Test the adjusted angle with a 1.5 mm straight pull, retaining the native grip and monitoring key motion against tactile shear.
The contact shifts during lifting still suggest binding. Reseat gently, then refine the angle between earlier pull tests rather than pulling farther.
Test this intermediate angle with a gentle 1.5 mm axial lift; hold grip and orientation fixed and compare tactile displacement.
Hold the small axial preload and probe the turning alignment in fine positive increments; check whether the displaced contacts recenter or develop stop deformation.
Maintain the small axial preload and continue fine positive turning toward resistance; watch for the contact displacement to relax at the extraction alignment.
Continue the fine positive turn without further lifting; look for the first clear torsional deformation or release of the existing axial preload.
The left contact has developed a flat edge consistent with torsional resistance. Confirm it with a very small further turn, holding height and grasp unchanged.
Both contacts now show opposing flattened edges, confirming torsional resistance. Unload a small amount of twist without changing the grasp or axial position before pulling straight.
Torsional flattening has relaxed. Test straight extraction at this near-stop angle, holding rotation and grip fixed while checking key motion and contact shear.
The upward pull still shifts the contacts. Hold height and turn gently toward resistance again; keep the stop alignment rather than backing away before the next pull.
Tactile flattening indicates the turning stop. Keep this angle rather than backing off and test a slow straight extraction, monitoring retention and axial slip.
The key has not clearly followed the lift. Hold height and cautiously continue the positive turn to characterize the stop rather than increasing extraction displacement.
Strong torsional deformation is visible, but the key has not followed the lift. Remove the axial preload straight downward while preserving the near-stop angle and grasp.
The reseated key shows strong opposing torsional deformation. Ease the twist back in small increments toward the onset of resistance, holding depth and grasp fixed.
Torsional clipping has relaxed. Pull straight upward at the current near-stop alignment, checking actual key motion rather than treating small contact shifts alone as failure.
Continue the straight pull a few millimeters at fixed angle and grasp to check whether the key follows; avoid another angle change while assessing axial motion.
The contact shift grew without clear key lift. Unload the 5 mm pull and ease the twist while returning to the seated depth; avoid further axial slip.
Apply only a small upward preload, then finely search the angle below the stop. Watch for the key to follow or tactile contacts to recenter rather than increasing pull distance.
Keep the small upward preload fixed and scan slightly below the current angle. Look for the key to rise and tactile contacts to return toward their seated positions.
Continue a systematic small-angle scan below the stop with height fixed. The key has not visibly followed the preload, so avoid further lifting until the contacts relax.
Keep the small axial preload unchanged and scan another small interval below the stop, monitoring for the key to rise instead of increasing pull displacement.
Continue scanning below the previously tested angles with height fixed; watch for release of the small axial preload rather than adding more lift.
Remove the axial preload completely before refining the turning stop; loaded angle scans have not released the key.
With axial load removed, return toward the positive turning limit. Earlier pull tests did not release the key, so reassess resistance before extracting.
Approach the resistance onset again with the key fully seated. Keep the native grasp and axial position fixed; refine the limit in smaller angular increments.
Advance only a small angle at the seated depth to identify the onset of stop deformation without adding axial load.
Keep the key fully seated and probe a little farther into the positive turn. Compare the onset and growth of tactile resistance before attempting another extraction.
Unload the visible torsional clipping and slightly reduce the gripper opening. Earlier straight pulls shifted the key across the pads without clear extraction; improve retention before retrying.
With torsional clipping relaxed and the opening reduced, retry a slow straight upward extraction. Keep this angle fixed and assess visible key motion and retention.
The key still appears seated while the contacts shift under lift. Remove the axial displacement, then recheck the turning limit with the reduced gripper opening.
Keep the key fully seated and continue a small positive turn. The current contacts are round; reassess resistance with the tighter opening before another straight pull.
The tighter grasp now shows rounded contact rather than clipping. Continue turning with the key seated, stopping to inspect the next tactile change.
Opposing flat tactile edges indicate torsional resistance with the tighter grasp. Relieve only a small amount of twist at fixed depth, then reassess before a straight pull.
Residual opposing flat edges remain after the first backoff. Relieve more torsion while keeping the key seated and grasp closed, then reassess for straight extraction.
Torsional deformation has relaxed at the new near-stop angle. Hold this orientation and closed grasp while pulling straight upward slowly; compare key motion and tactile retention.
The pads shifted during lifting without clear key motion. Hold height and approach the turning limit in fine increments with the closed grasp; watch for axial release before pulling farther.
Maintain the current height and closed grasp; approach the stop by a small additional turn. Avoid backing away before checking a straight pull at the resistance onset.
The tactile edges now indicate resistance. Hold this angle and closed grasp, and continue straight upward to test release without another angular backoff.

The contacts show substantial axial displacement and torsional clipping. Remove the lift and ease a small amount of twist, returning fully to the seated depth before testing the intermediate alignment.
